figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: one journey - modulate, propagate, receive, and count the noise
figures.read: every result is a bandwidth, a modulation index, a range formula, or Shannon's ceiling

figures.title: The three-part system: modulate, send, demodulate
figures.why: every communication question walks the same chain; fix the stages
figures.data: source → modulator → transmitter → channel(+noise) → receiver → demodulator → destination
figures.read: the modulator stamps the message on a carrier, the channel adds noise, the demodulator unstamps it

figures.title: Propagation: three modes, three frequency bands
figures.why: the propagation question is decided by frequency alone
figures.data: ground < 2 MHz; sky 2-30 MHz; space > 30 MHz with range √(2Rh)
figures.read: low frequencies hug the Earth, mid bounce off the ionosphere, high must see their target

figures.title: AM: the envelope carries the message - until it inverts
figures.why: amplitude modulation is read from the envelope; the index is its dial
figures.data: μ = (Amax-Amin)/(Amax+Amin); μ≤1 required; power efficiency μ²/(2+μ²)
figures.read: keep the index at or under one, or the envelope folds and the message is lost

figures.title: Shannon's ceiling: bandwidth × signal-to-noise
figures.why: no scheme can beat the capacity formula; every design is measured against it
figures.data: C = B log2(1+S/N); P_n = kTB; 30 dB → 10 bits/s/Hz
figures.read: more bandwidth or signal buys capacity, but logarithmically

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the route before any number is touched
figures.read: frequency picks the propagation mode, a waveform picks the index, capacity stops at Shannon
